title: Muscle Weakness
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness, myalgias, and fatigue. History reveals concurrent use of simvastatin and gemfibrozil — a CONTRAINDICATED combination. Gemfibrozil inhibits CYP2C8 and OATP1B1, dramatically increasing simvastatin levels → myotoxicity. Labs show markedly elevated CK (often >10x ULN). UA shows myoglobinuria (risk of AKI). Differentiate from other causes: hypothyroidism, polymyositis, alcohol myopathy, steroid myopathy. Management: IMMEDIATELY discontinue simvastatin and gemfibrozil. Aggressive IV fluids to prevent pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis. Monitor renal function and electrolytes (hyperkalemia risk from muscle breakdown). Alternative lipid management after recovery: atorvastatin or rosuvastatin (metabolized differently, less interaction risk), ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitor. Fenofibrate (not gemfibrozil) can be used with statins with caution.
